name: Node.js
one_liner: The JavaScript runtime essentially all frontend tooling runs on.
what_it_is: A JavaScript runtime built on V8 with an event-driven, non-blocking I/O model. For frontend developers it matters less as a server platform than as the thing every build tool, linter and test runner executes inside.
why_it_matters: Node is infrastructure you rarely choose but constantly depend on, and its version is a recurring source of "works on my machine". Knowing which release line is current LTS, and pinning it per project, prevents a category of build failure that is tedious to diagnose — as this repository demonstrates, its 2016-era build no longer installs on a current Node at all.
suitable_for: Running frontend build tooling — effectively non-optional
Server-side JavaScript with mature operational support
not_suitable_for: CPU-bound workloads, which block its event loop
Situations where a single-binary toolchain would be simpler than a Node install plus dependencies
